Leibniz and Pascal Triangles

CountingSequencesAlgorithms
Game: Two famous triangles hide patterns when you keep only the remainders.
How to play: Choose Pascal or Leibniz, then change the number of rows and the modulus.

Look for the math

Pascal's triangle adds the two numbers above; Leibniz's adds the two below. Reducing either one modulo n reveals surprising repeating patterns.

Two related triangles

The m-th entry of Pascal's row n is the binomial coefficient C(n, m). The matching entry of the Leibniz harmonic triangle is the reciprocal of (n + 1)C(n, m). Pascal builds by addition from the top, Leibniz by subtraction from the bottom — yet both are symmetric.

Telescoping diagonals

The second diagonal of the Leibniz triangle is 1/2, 1/6, 1/12, 1/20, … = 1/(n(n+1)), whose sum telescopes to 1: each term is 1/n − 1/(n+1). The page's other identity, 1/2 = 1/3 + 1/12 + 1/30 + …, is the next diagonal. The logic test checks the row sums of Pascal, both symmetry properties and these sums.

Set the modulus to 2. What shape does Pascal's triangle become?
